item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US housing starts fell -5.2% MoM in September, to an annualized rate of 1.22 million, the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US housing starts fell -5.2% MoM in September, to an annualized rate of 1.22 million, the 2nd-lowest reading since May 2020.
This follows MoM declines of -4.9% and -5.9% in July and August.
Single-family housing starts dropped -4.6% MoM last month, to 859,000, the 2nd-lowest since April 2023.
At the same time, multifamily housing starts fell -7.2%, to 349,000, the 2nd-lowest since May 2025.
Higher mortgage rates and worsening affordability are heavily weighing on housing demand.
Furthermore, elevated housing inventories and falling homebuilder confidence are discouraging new construction.
The US housing market is frozen.

item.title: @cultured: Whop has raised $200M in Series D funding at a $5.1B valuation, backed by @sequoia and @shopify. It...
item.dc:creator: @cultured
item.description:
Whop has raised $200M in Series D funding at a $5.1B valuation, backed by @sequoia and @shopify.
It really feels like we are barely touching the tip of the iceberg in a market larger than anyone can imagine.
We first launched Whop as a better way for us to sell sneaker bots, one of the most niche types of desktop software out there.
Total TAM? Probably $20,000 per day.
Who cares, tiny market.
But, what people discounted is the idea that there were actually 70,000 other markets exactly like that one.
Beyond the investment itself, I am especially excited to welcome legendary silicon valley investor @dougleone to our board of directors. Doug and the sequoia team are nothing but a brilliant, resourceful, and principled group of people.
My co-founder Cameron and I started building on Shopify when we were 13 years old. Shopify is one of the most impactful all-in-one cloud ecosystems ever created; @tobi has pioneered modern entrepreneurship the way we know it and we are thrilled to have him in our corner.
We have a tenet at Whop to be the dumbest in the room and I am very grateful that this has recently become a lot easier.
We are focused on markets, scale economies, and progressive media. If that is up your alley, please message me directly.
The $200M raised will support our expansion as we build economic infrastructure for the next century, continuing on our mission of delivering everyone an income.

Who cares, tiny market.

But, what people discounted is the idea that there were actually 70,000 other markets exactly like that one.

Beyond the investment itself, I am especially excited to welcome legendary silicon valley investor @dougleone to our board of directors. Doug and the sequoia team are nothing but a brilliant, resourceful, and principled group of people.

My co-founder Cameron and I started building on Shopify when we were 13 years old. Shopify is one of the most impactful all-in-one cloud ecosystems ever created; @tobi has pioneered modern entrepreneurship the way we know it and we are thrilled to have him in our corner.

We have a tenet at Whop to be the dumbest in the room and I am very grateful that this has recently become a lot easier.

The $200M raised will support our expansion as we build economic infrastructure for the next century, continuing on our mission of delivering everyone an income.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI-related borrowing is skyrocketing. US Dollar-denominated AI-related corporate bond issuance is u...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI-related borrowing is skyrocketing.
US Dollar-denominated AI-related corporate bond issuance is up to $419 billion so far in 2026, the highest annual figure on record.
This represents a +90% YoY increase from full-year 2025 and a +437% increase from full-year 2024.
Year-to-date, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, and Oracle, $ORCL, have issued a combined $157 billion in corporate bonds, accounting for 37% of the total.
This is followed by investment-grade and high-yield data center and computing companies, which have raised $66 billion and $37 billion, respectively, and together account for ~25% of AI-related issuance.
Other AI-linked corporate bonds have represented $159 billion, or 38%.
The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Tokenization is accelerating.
There are now over 360 onchain tokenized equity products, up +200% YTD.
10 of these products have exceeded $100 million in tokenized supply.
As we saw this weekend, demand for 24/7 access to equities is rapidly expanding.
In fact, the majority of volume in these tokenized products, at ~60%, is currently taking place outside of regular market hours.
Today, onchain giant Jupiter, a leader in this space, reported a +215% quarter-over-quarter jump in tokenized equity trade count.
We expect more record highs ahead in this space.

item.title: @wallstengine: NVIDIA & VERTIV TARGET UP TO 30% MORE AI TOKENS WITH THE SAME CAPACITY $NVDA and $VRT announced a n...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NVIDIA & VERTIV TARGET UP TO 30% MORE AI TOKENS WITH THE SAME CAPACITY
$NVDA and $VRT announced a new AI factory deployment approach at GTC Berlin that could cut the time from project kickoff to productive capacity from 120 days to just 48 days.
According to Vertiv's modeled estimates, this could result in up to 30% more cumulative AI token output in the first 12 months, without increasing installed computing capacity.
Here's how the new approach works:
• 10x Faster Design: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory reference design, Omniverse DSX Blueprint, and Vertiv's SimReady assets integrate with Dassault Systèmes' 3DEXPERIENCE platform to reduce configuration and validation time from 30 days to just 3 days.
• 50% Faster Deployment: Vertiv's prefabricated OneCore and SmartRun infrastructure could reduce on-site power and cooling deployment from 90 days to 45 days.
• 72 Days Saved: Combined, the approach could bring AI factories online approximately 10 weeks earlier, providing 317 productive days in the first year compared with 245 using conventional methods.
• Real-World Deployment: Polar Data Centers is applying Vertiv's factory-built approach to the first 41 MW phase of its AI data center in Herøya, Norway 🇳🇴, with plans to scale the facility to 100 MW.
• Factory-Built Infrastructure: Power, cooling, networking, and supporting systems can be designed and virtually validated before construction, with more assembly and testing completed off-site.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: This is unprecedented. Micron, $MU, and Nvidia, $NVDA are expected to account for 36% of the S&P 50...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
This is unprecedented.
Micron, $MU, and Nvidia, $NVDA are expected to account for 36% of the S&P 500’s earnings growth in Q3 2026 earnings season.
This comes as $MU and $NVDA are expected to contribute +5.2 and +4.6 percentage points to the index’s +27% YoY earnings growth, respectively.
Meanwhile, the next 8 top contributors are projected to add +8.2 percentage points, accounting for ~30% of the estimated S&P 500’s net income growth.
Then, the remaining 490 stocks are set to contribute just +9.2 percentage points, representing 34% of the index’s projected earnings growth.
Excluding those top 10 contributors, earnings growth is estimated to decline -11% YoY in Q3.
Never in history have we witnessed market concentration like this.

item.title: @wallstengine: AGILE ROBOTS UNVEILS NVIDIA-POWERED HUMANOID, TARGETS UP TO 2,000 ROBOTS IN 2027 Germany's 🇩🇪 Agi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
AGILE ROBOTS UNVEILS NVIDIA-POWERED HUMANOID, TARGETS UP TO 2,000 ROBOTS IN 2027
Germany's 🇩🇪 Agile Robots unveiled Agile ONE SN at $NVDA's GTC Berlin, a new humanoid robot built for AI research and development.
CEO Zhaopeng Chen told Reuters the company plans to produce between 1,000 and 2,000 humanoid robots across its ONE S and ONE SN models in 2027, with production expected to begin by the end of 2026.
Here are the key features:
• Size: Stands 1.4 meters (4.6 feet) tall and weighs 40 kg (88 lbs), according to NVIDIA, with 31 degrees of freedom and a 3 kg payload per arm.
• Hands: Two five-fingered WUJI Hand 2 robotic hands, each with 20 degrees of freedom, tactile sensing, and 1kHz force control for precise manipulation.
• AI Computing: Powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor, delivering 2,070 FP4 teraflops of compute and 128GB of unified memory for onboard reasoning and real-time control.
• Vision and Sensors: Equipped with head and wrist cameras, lidar sensors, and inertial measurement units to perceive and interact with its environment.
• AI Software: Comes preconfigured with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, providing AI models and tools for robot learning, training, and whole-body control.
• Safety: Planned integration with NVIDIA Halos to support safer robot operation and deployment.
• Development: NVIDIA says the preconfigured platform can reduce setup time for researchers from weeks to days.
• Availability: Expected in early 2027, with Stanford University and ETH Zurich among institutions showing interest.
“The breakthrough for humanoids is usefulness at scale,” CEO Zhaopeng Chen said.

item.title: @wallstengine: GOOGLE CLOUD & NVIDIA PLAN TO SCALE VERA RUBIN INFRASTRUCTURE TO UP TO 960,000 GPUS Google Cloud an...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
GOOGLE CLOUD & NVIDIA PLAN TO SCALE VERA RUBIN INFRASTRUCTURE TO UP TO 960,000 GPUS
Google Cloud announced that its new A5X instances, powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, will become generally available next month, with plans to expand availability to Europe.
The new infrastructure is designed to support large-scale AI training, inference, autonomous AI agents, and reinforcement learning.
Here's what was announced:
• 960,000 Rubin GPUs: Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin infrastructure to as many as 960,000 GPUs across multiple data center sites.
• A5X Instances: Combine NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud's Virgo networking, and fourth-generation liquid cooling to support demanding AI workloads.
• Ineffable Intelligence: The company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver became the first customer to access A5X, using it to develop "superlearners" that continuously improve through experience.
• WPP: Tested AI-powered creative workflows using NVIDIA Nemotron and OpenShell on A5X. Initial tests showed that workloads previously requiring a multi-node cluster could run on a single A5X instance.
• Confidential Computing: Google Cloud is also expanding secure AI infrastructure, making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with plans to bring rack-scale capabilities to GB300 NVL72-powered A4X Max instances.
Google Cloud and NVIDIA are also exploring new power-efficiency technologies through NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS to support larger AI deployments within existing data center power limits.

• Confidential Computing: Google Cloud is also expanding secure AI infrastructure, making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with plans to bring rack-scale capabilities to GB300 NVL72-powered A4X Max instances.

Google Cloud and NVIDIA are also exploring new power-efficiency technologies through NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS to support larger AI deployments within existing data center power limits.

item.title: @wallstengine: NVIDIA & AMKOR $AMKR PLAN OVER 300% EXPANSION IN ADVANCED PACKAGING CAPACITY NVIDIA announced new a...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NVIDIA & AMKOR $AMKR PLAN OVER 300% EXPANSION IN ADVANCED PACKAGING CAPACITY
NVIDIA announced new agreements with major semiconductor supply chain partners at GTC Berlin to expand manufacturing capacity for its current and next-generation AI platforms.
Here's what's planned:
• Amkor: Increase advanced packaging interposer wafer capacity in South Korea by more than 300% by the end of 2028, alongside new manufacturing facilities.
• IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Unimicron: Expand substrate capacity by 2.5x over the next three years, with production expansions across Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan.
• KYEC: Build new semiconductor testing facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. High-volume production is targeted for April 2027.
• SPIL: Increase optical-engine manufacturing capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with plans to double it again by the end of 2028.
• Semiconductor Testing: NVIDIA expects its overall testing capacity to double from 2026 to 2027, supported by expansions in the U.S., Taiwan, and Singapore.
Jensen Huang said:
“We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint.”
The expansion is intended to increase production capacity and strengthen NVIDIA's global supply chain as demand for AI infrastructure continues to grow.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA ANNOUNCES MAJOR EXPANSION OF ITS ISAAC ROBOTICS PLATFORM, INCLUDING A NEW HUMANOID ROBOT “the...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA ANNOUNCES MAJOR EXPANSION OF ITS ISAAC ROBOTICS PLATFORM, INCLUDING A NEW HUMANOID ROBOT
“the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching.”
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA introduced new humanoid robotics technology, AI training tools, simulation datasets, and software designed to accelerate the development of general-purpose robots.
Here's what's new:
• Agile ONE SN: A new humanoid reference robot developed by Agile Robots, powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor and Isaac GR00T. It stands 1.4 meters tall, weighs 40 kg, features 31 degrees of freedom, and has two five-finger hands. Expected in early 2027.
• Isaac Lab 3.0: Now generally available, enabling developers to train and refine robot behaviors using multi-GPU workflows and physics-based simulation.
• Isaac OS: A new open-source runtime connecting AI models, sensors, controls, and robot hardware for real-time operation.
• New Training Data: More than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, alongside the Human 1M Dataset containing human activity videos and 3D hand-tracking data.
• DGX Station: Three new open-source workflows for improving GR00T models through reinforcement learning, developing complex manipulation skills, and generating synthetic training data using NVIDIA Cosmos.
Companies including ABB Robotics, KUKA, NEURA Robotics, Universal Robots, Hexagon Robotics, Humanoid, and Sereact are building on NVIDIA's technologies for industrial robotics applications.

item.title: @wallstengine: Jensen Huang says NVIDIA's DSX POD could cut the time from AI hardware arrival to producing tokens...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Jensen Huang says NVIDIA's DSX POD could cut the time from AI hardware arrival to producing tokens from four to five months down to about one month.
He says a one-gigawatt AI data center costs $50 billion and is expected to generate $40 billion in annual revenue, meaning a three-month delay could cost $10 billion in revenue.
“$10 billion worth of revenues will make anybody anxious.”
Jensen explained:
“And so by moving this into the supply chain, the speed by which we can turn on go from installation, arrival of computing to production of tokens will go from many months. We think something along the lines of 4 to 5 months down to about a month.”
“Okay, so this is a complete transformation of the world's supply chain and this will change the way that people install and build data centers.”
“And hopefully as a result, velocity goes up, the wasted idle compute, the wasted idle CapEx will reduce and everybody becomes more profitable.”

item.title: @wallstengine: Jensen Huang just showed how NVIDIA and Anthropic are working together to make AI agents more secur...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Jensen Huang just showed how NVIDIA and Anthropic are working together to make AI agents more secure with $NVDA OpenShell and Claude Managed Agents.
OpenShell allows AI agents to operate inside secure sandboxes while controlling exactly what they can access and do.
Here's how it works:
• Controls which files, tools, networks, and private data AI agents can access.
• Blocks actions by default unless explicitly permitted by security policies.
• Monitors agent activity and logs every allowed or blocked action.
• Allows companies to run agent execution inside their own infrastructure, keeping sensitive data and code within their environment.
• Uses a policy prover to mathematically verify what resources an agent can access.
With Claude Managed Agents, Anthropic handles agent orchestration while NVIDIA OpenShell adds security controls inside the execution environment.
NVIDIA OpenShell is open source, while Claude Managed Agents is available in public beta.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The 15 largest S&P 500 stocks now account for a record 46.7% of the index’s market value....
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The 15 largest S&P 500 stocks now account for a record 46.7% of the index’s market value.
By comparison, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, the 15 largest stocks accounted for 27.2% of the S&P 500.
The remaining 485 stocks represent just 53.3% of the S&P 500’s market cap.
This comes as Nvidia, $NVDA, Apple, $AAPL, Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, account for 7.5%, 7.1%, 5.9%, and 5.6%, respectively, or 26.1% combined.
This means just 4 stocks account for more than the next 11 combined.
Furthermore, the combined market cap of the 5 largest stocks now equals that of the bottom 434 stocks in the index, the largest gap on record.
Market concentration is at historic extremes.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The global debt crisis has never been worse. Japan now has a gross government Debt-to-GDP ratio of...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The global debt crisis has never been worse.
Japan now has a gross government Debt-to-GDP ratio of 204.4%, the highest among any major world economy.
Italy follows at 138.4%, while the United States stands at 125.8%, which is only below the ~132.0% record set during the 2020 pandemic.
At the same time, France’s gross government Debt-to-GDP ratio is 118.4%, while Canada’s, China’s, and the UK’s are 110.7%, 106.9%, and 103.6%, respectively.
By comparison, Germany is the only major economy below 100.0%, at 64.6%.
The current average among advanced economies is 108.2%.
The world economy is drowning in debt.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US affordability crisis is worsening: Food prices have surged +34.5% since December 2019, now a...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US affordability crisis is worsening:
Food prices have surged +34.5% since December 2019, now at their highest level on record.
Rent and grocery prices have risen +33.3% and +30.0%, respectively.
Furthermore, motor vehicle maintenance and repair prices have soared +55.2% over the same period.
Meanwhile, prices for services excluding rent, including medical care, transportation, education, communication, and recreation, have increased +29.2% since December 2019.
As a result, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) has risen +30.4%.
Basic necessities are becoming increasingly unaffordable in the US.

Why Hedge Funds Are Getting Blindsided By This Market
🔊
On The Macro Show this morning, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough and Director of Research Daryl Jones @HedgeyeDJ covered why factors are wreaking havoc on hedge funds.
The spark was Citadel’s head of global equities, Justin Lobell, noting that even though the S&P hasn’t moved much, it’s the factor moves getting people offsides and blowing up books.
One of the first charts Hedgeye ever built 18 years ago was factors, and those moves have crushed people.
For Keith, it’s non-negotiable.
As he put it, “if you don’t have factors on your screens,” rather than something like the Dow and points, “you should not be gainfully employed.”
No NHL player uses a wooden stick and nobody takes a horse and buggy to work, yet in markets people still lean on moving averages and valuation models instead of factors, flows, and gamma.
The managers who wouldn’t evolve are effectively extinct, and however this AI bubble ends, loaded with levered ETFs and short-dated options, factors will be the defining feature of it.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Beacon has launched an open-source memory system for AI coding agents, alongside a $5.5 million seed round announced by its team.
The software captures coding sessions and converts useful debugging patterns, fixes and corrections into reusable skills. It supports more than 20 coding tools, including Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
Beacon uses decision models such as Jev to identify information worth retaining. Developers can also start a task in Claude Code and continue it in Codex with one command, transferring context between tools. https://x.com/jqdsouza/status/2112552451547001218/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US electricity prices are skyrocketing. The average price of US residential electricity has risen +...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US electricity prices are skyrocketing.
The average price of US residential electricity has risen +11% since January 2025, to 19.6 cents per kilowatt-hour in August 2026, near an all-time high.
Average prices during the first 8 months of 2026 were +40% higher than in the same period of 2019.
The largest increase in residential electricity prices over this period was in Maine, at +90%, followed by California and New York, at nearly +70%.
This comes as the AI boom is intensifying electricity demand, with data centers requiring enormous amounts of electricity to power thousands of chips and cooling systems.
A 1-gigawatt data center can consume as much electricity as 800,000 homes.
As a result, wholesale electricity prices in areas near significant data center activity surged by as much as +267% between 2020 and 2025.
The AI revolution is driving a surge in electricity demand, and households are increasingly feeling the cost.

item.title: @wallstengine: CHINESE TECH GIANTS REPORTEDLY ORDER OVER $35B IN $NVDA AI CHIPS ByteDance, Alibaba $BABA and Tence...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CHINESE TECH GIANTS REPORTEDLY ORDER OVER $35B IN $NVDA AI CHIPS
ByteDance, Alibaba $BABA and Tencent have reportedly placed orders for more than 3M Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 GPUs as U.S. export restrictions limit access to more advanced AI processors.
The export-compliant chips cost around $11,400 each and are primarily designed for AI inference workloads.
Total Chinese orders reportedly exceed 6M GPUs, while Nvidia expects to produce no more than 3M globally in 2027 as manufacturing capacity shifts toward its next-generation Rubin chips.
Nvidia has warned partners they may receive just 5-10% of requested quantities, with commercial shipments expected to begin in Q1 2027.
The reported order values do not represent confirmed sales or guaranteed deliveries.
Source: Reuters.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META'S PROMETHEUS AI SUPERCLUSTER NOW CONNECTS HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF NVIDIA GPUS, WITH 1 MILLIO...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META'S PROMETHEUS AI SUPERCLUSTER NOW CONNECTS HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF NVIDIA GPUS, WITH 1 MILLION PLANNED
Meta has completed the first phase of its gigawatt-scale Prometheus supercluster in Ohio, which was used to train its latest Muse Wonder AI models.
The system combines NVIDIA $NVDA GB200 and GB300 NVL72 platforms across multiple interconnected buildings, operating as a single large-scale training system.
Meta says it has reduced training interruptions by 99% from their peak, following extensive engineering work with NVIDIA on hardware reliability, networking and firmware.
The company reported more than 85% productive training time for Muse Wonder pretraining and over 90% for reinforcement learning.
Meta plans to expand the cluster further with NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin systems, continuing its buildout of infrastructure for frontier AI models.
Source: Meta Engineering.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Corporate earnings growth is set to slow: 10 of the 11 sectors in the S&P 500 are estimated to reco...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Corporate earnings growth is set to slow:
10 of the 11 sectors in the S&P 500 are estimated to record lower YoY earnings growth in Q3 2026, compared to Q2.
The Consumer Discretionary sector is expected to post the largest slowdown, from +91% YoY in Q2 to just +2% YoY in Q3.
This is followed by Communication Services, with projected Q3 earnings growth at +66%, down from +126%.
Earnings growth in the Financials sector is estimated to decrease to +2.4% from +22.3%.
Energy and Information Technology, the two best-performing S&P 500 sectors, are expected to see earnings growth decline from +147.8% to +122.5% and from +77.9% to +65.9%, respectively.
We are set for an eventful earnings season.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: China’s trade surplus jumped +$67 billion YoY in the first 9 months of 2026, or +7.7%, to...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: China’s trade surplus jumped +$67 billion YoY in the first 9 months of 2026, or +7.7%, to a record $938 billion.
This marks its 3rd consecutive YoY increase for this period of the year, totalling +$318 billion.
In September alone, China's trade surplus rose +$50 billion YoY, or +51%, to $134 billion, its 2nd-largest on record.
Exports soared +36% YoY and imports jumped +31%.
At the same time, high-tech shipments surged +64% YoY, accounting for ~50% of total export growth, as global AI infrastructure demand boosted hardware exports.
China’s trade surplus is now on track to exceed the $1.2 trillion record set in 2025.
China is expanding global trade at an unprecedented pace.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Average domestic round-trip fares for Thanksgiving are up +31% YoY, to $402, the highest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Average domestic round-trip fares for Thanksgiving are up +31% YoY, to $402, the highest in at least 10 years.
This marks the 3rd consecutive annual increase, totaling +$133, or +49%.
Since the 2020 pandemic, average domestic round-trip fares for Thanksgiving travel have more than doubled.
By comparison, average round-trip airfares for Christmas are up +23% YoY.
This comes as jet fuel prices have risen +91% since the Iran War began, to ~$4.50 per gallon, driving up airlines’ operating costs.
Americans are facing their priciest holiday travel season in years.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US margin debt jumped +$26 billion in September, to $1.48 trillion, the 2nd-highest level...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US margin debt jumped +$26 billion in September, to $1.48 trillion, the 2nd-highest level on record.
Since the start of 2026, margin debt has surged +$255 billion, or +21%.
As a % of GDP, this metric is up to a record 4.5%, surpassing the previous peak of 3.6% set in 2021.
At the same time, the margin debt-to-M2 money supply ratio is up to 6.3%, the 3rd-highest level on record.
By comparison, this ratio peaked at 6.4% during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.
Leveraged investing has never been more popular.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US semiconductor stocks are experiencing massive volatility: The Semiconductor Index, SOX, to S&P 5...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US semiconductor stocks are experiencing massive volatility:
The Semiconductor Index, SOX, to S&P 500 ratio is down to 1.45 points, its lowest since April 2026.
This ratio has declined -0.46 points, or -24%, from its mid-June peak.
Over this period, SOX has fallen -24%, while the S&P 500 has gained +2%.
The relative decline is comparable to the one seen following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst.
However, the ratio is still up +142% since the 2022 bear market low of 0.60.
Meanwhile, SOX has also declined for 8 consecutive trading sessions, its longest streak since the 2008 Financial Crisis.
Semiconductor stocks are more volatile than ever.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US equity market's bull run shows no signs of slowing down: The S&P 500 has recorded 124 all-ti...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US equity market's bull run shows no signs of slowing down:
The S&P 500 has recorded 124 all-time highs since the current bull market began on October 12th, 2022.
Over this period, the index has rallied +118%, entering the 5th year of its bull market.
This year alone, the index has posted 28 all-time highs, after 39 and 57 in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
By comparison, the S&P 500 recorded 70 all-time highs in 2021 and 33 in 2020.
Meanwhile, more than 1,003 trading days have passed since the S&P 500 last recorded a new 52-week low, marking the 6th-longest such streak in history.
For perspective, such a streak lasted 2,556 days between 1990 and 2000, ending on November 21st.
The market is experiencing a historic bull run.

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC COMMITS 5% OF ITS SHARES TO PUBLIC BENEFIT FUND, WITH ADDITIONAL PLEDGES TIED TO VALUATIO...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC COMMITS 5% OF ITS SHARES TO PUBLIC BENEFIT FUND, WITH ADDITIONAL PLEDGES TIED TO VALUATION GROWTH
Anthropic announced the creation of the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, designed to support charitable initiatives and address the broader societal impact of AI, including its effects on jobs.
The initial equity contribution is subject to stockholder approval. The board may also allocate an additional 2% of shares for every 50% increase in the company’s valuation above an undisclosed baseline.
Anthropic says its total public-benefit commitments now represent roughly 20% of company equity when combined with its founders’ existing pledge to donate 80% of their personal stakes and its employee donation-matching program.
The company has already committed $200M toward studying and addressing AI’s impact on employment.
The fund will operate as a wholly owned LLC, with its shares prohibited from being used for lobbying or political contributions.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Japanese banks sold -$16 billion of foreign bonds in September, their largest monthly sal...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Japanese banks sold -$16 billion of foreign bonds in September, their largest monthly sale since February.
This also marks their 9th consecutive monthly sale, the longest streak since 2022.
As a result, sales of foreign debt by Japanese banks in the first 9 months of 2026 were the largest for that period since 2005.
Japanese financial institutions have turned to domestic government bonds, whose yields have surged to their highest levels in 3 decades.
Over the 5 months ending in August, large banks and insurers bought +$34 billion of Japanese government bonds with maturities of 2 years or more, their largest 5-month purchase since the start of 2023.
Global bond demand is undergoing a historic shift as yields rise.
item.content:encoded:
BREAKING: Japanese banks sold -$16 billion of foreign bonds in September, their largest monthly sale since February.

This also marks their 9th consecutive monthly sale, the longest streak since 2022.

As a result, sales of foreign debt by Japanese banks in the first 9 months of 2026 were the largest for that period since 2005.

Japanese financial institutions have turned to domestic government bonds, whose yields have surged to their highest levels in 3 decades.

Over the 5 months ending in August, large banks and insurers bought +$34 billion of Japanese government bonds with maturities of 2 years or more, their largest 5-month purchase since the start of 2023.

Global bond demand is undergoing a historic shift as yields rise.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Global smartphone purchases have collapsed. Worldwide smartphone shipments dropped -22.0% YoY in Q3...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Global smartphone purchases have collapsed.
Worldwide smartphone shipments dropped -22.0% YoY in Q3 2026, to 255.3 million units, their largest quarterly decline on record.
Samsung's shipments fell -5.8% YoY, to 57.8 million units, while Apple's declined -4.0% to 57.3 million units.
At the same time, Xiaomi shipments fell -29.2% YoY to 30.7 million units, Oppo dropped -34.5%, to 25.6 million units, while Vivo fell -31.5%, to 19.1 million units.
This comes as memory costs have surged +350% since last year, driven by AI-related demand, putting further pressure on smartphone manufacturers.
As a result, soaring component costs are forcing vendors to raise prices and reduce budget-focused offerings, with consumers increasingly keeping their existing devices for longer.
Global smartphone sales are contracting amid surging prices.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The number of restaurants in New York dropped ~2,000 YoY in Q1 2026, posting its largest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The number of restaurants in New York dropped ~2,000 YoY in Q1 2026, posting its largest YoY decline in at least 36 years.
This surpasses even the worst contraction recorded in any quarter during the 2020 pandemic.
The number of eating and drinking places in New York State has now declined YoY for 4 consecutive quarters, its longest streak since 2021.
This comes as restaurants are facing surging operating expenses, including insurance premiums, wages, interest rates, utilities, and health coverage, with overall costs rising faster than national averages.
Last year, employee health insurance costs jumped +12.9% for New York-area service firms, business insurance rose +7.0%, while utility costs surged +8.5%, according to the Manhattan Chamber of Commerce.
Skyrocketing costs are crushing New York restaurants.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Non-asset owners are seeing a large drop in US consumer sentiment. Since January 2026, consumer sen...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Non-asset owners are seeing a large drop in US consumer sentiment.
Since January 2026, consumer sentiment is down -27% among the bottom 33% of stockholders, the largest decline among the stock-wealth groups surveyed.
This is followed by those who do not own stocks, whose sentiment is down -25% over the same period.
By comparison, sentiment is down just -9% among the middle 33% and -7% among the top 33% of stockholders.
Asset ownership has helped offset the impact of higher living costs, leaving consumers with fewer or no stocks more exposed to the recent acceleration in inflation.
Meanwhile, 1-year consumer inflation expectations rose +0.1 percentage point this month, to 4.7%, its 2nd-highest reading since August 2025.
Own assets or be left behind.

item.title: @Mike_Taylor1972: The problem with data ctr collateral, rev recognition, neg pricing and $NVDA: Debt is “Secured”: Mu...
item.dc:creator: @Mike_Taylor1972
item.description:
The problem with data ctr collateral, rev recognition, neg pricing and $NVDA:
Debt is “Secured”: Much neocloud debt is secured with a guarantee net-net by $NVDA. The collateral is the GPUs themselves.
Rev Recognition “oops I did it again”: Imagine $NVDA projects 100 units sold (at 100% growth) for 2027. BUT what if for one reason or another, only 60 get placed into slowly-assembled data ctrs? Production, pricing and scarcity of supply abruptly ends if the parabolic build of data centers slow.
Negative Pricing begins for GPUs, memory …and importantly, the collateral.
The Collateral of that data ctr loan is a GPU that now has LOWER value as supply constraint abates.
In fact, that collateral is terrible, as if one calls in on any, they ALL tank in value, accelerating the daisy chain.
What worries me greatly, is as I have pointed this out to my peers, very few have thought this through. “Yeah but it’s $NVDA, a $5trn company”. My only answer: “NOT if datactr growth is slowing, bc they will immediately lose pricing power, margins, and are on the hook for SOOOO much collateral, it’s mind bending”
Side note: There is NO government rescue for this one.
Now- get in there and tell me how I am an idiot. Beware, there is a queue!

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Interest expense on US public debt rose +$144 billion YoY in FY2026, or +12%, to a record...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Interest expense on US public debt rose +$144 billion YoY in FY2026, or +12%, to a record $1.36 trillion.
This marks the 6th consecutive annual increase, for a total of +$839 billion, or +161%.
For perspective, total receipts rose just +3.2% YoY, to $5.40 trillion.
In other words, interest on federal debt accounted for 25% of total US government receipts.
Meanwhile, Social Security, the largest government expense, jumped +$86 billion YoY, or +5.5%, to a record $1.67 trillion.
At this pace, interest costs will exceed Social Security as the largest government outlay by the end of 2028.
What is the long-term plan here?

item.description:
BREAKING: The US deficit widened to $1.99 trillion for FY2026, up +12% from the $1.78 trillion recorded last year.
Spending rose by +6%, to $7.4 trillion, and NET interest officially rose above $1 trillion.
Debt servicing costs are now their third largest expense for the US government, only behind Social Security and Medicare.
This marks the fourth-straight year with the US fiscal deficit around $2 trillion.
The deficit spending crisis is out of control.

Boston Dynamics spinout Dynamic Creatures is introducing robot characters designed to roam theme parks, hotels and resorts and interact with guests in real time.
Its SnowJay AI platform coordinates how the robots move, perceive their surroundings and respond.
The team uses motion capture and reinforcement learning to teach natural movement, with professional puppeteers helping shape the characters’ expressions.
The goal is for each character to adapt to the person in front of it as the interaction unfolds.
Dynamic Creatures is Boston Dynamics’ official hospitality and entertainment partner.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Tesla’s Roadster Is Just Another Publicity Stunt 🔊 Hedgeye Industrials analyst Jack Cromwell broke...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Tesla’s Roadster Is Just Another Publicity Stunt
🔊
Hedgeye Industrials analyst Jack Cromwell broke down Tesla's new Roadster unveil on The Call @ Hedgeye this morning.
The reveal was pure spectacle. The car drove upside down, hit 60mph in under a second, and flew on rocket-style thrusters, which Cromwell called "all very cool and all very unrealistic for actual use."
The stock was up about 3% pre-market, which the team pegged as the retail crowd, since any serious investor can see this isn't a future earnings boost.
The more interesting angle is why launch now, after nearly a decade of delay.
The Roadster was built in collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, which may be Musk hinting at interest in a merger, something he'd likely try to push through before the end of the Trump administration and which would simplify things administratively.
The bottom line from our team's perspective: cool to watch, but "just another publicity stunt" that adds little to nothing for Tesla shareholders and shouldn't move the stock.
Subscribe to The Call @ Hedgeye for daily market insights from our team of 40+ analysts: https://insights.hedgeye.com/the-call/

🔊

The reveal was pure spectacle. The car drove upside down, hit 60mph in under a second, and flew on rocket-style thrusters, which Cromwell called "all very cool and all very unrealistic for actual use."

The stock was up about 3% pre-market, which the team pegged as the retail crowd, since any serious investor can see this isn't a future earnings boost.

The more interesting angle is why launch now, after nearly a decade of delay.

The Roadster was built in collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, which may be Musk hinting at interest in a merger, something he'd likely try to push through before the end of the Trump administration and which would simplify things administratively.

The bottom line from our team's perspective: cool to watch, but "just another publicity stunt" that adds little to nothing for Tesla shareholders and shouldn't move the stock.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The last 48 hours have been very telling. After US CPI inflation rose to 3.7% on Wednesday, the 10Y...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The last 48 hours have been very telling.
After US CPI inflation rose to 3.7% on Wednesday, the 10Y Note Yield surged to 5.33%.
~24 hours later, it was -30 basis points lower as the S&P 500 and technology stocks sold off.
Today, yields are back on the rise as equity markets recover.
The ONLY thing that has materially pushed yields lower over the last 2 months has been a downturn in stocks.
Will the Trump Administration soon be forced to pick between the equity and bond market?
item.content:encoded:
The last 48 hours have been very telling.

After US CPI inflation rose to 3.7% on Wednesday, the 10Y Note Yield surged to 5.33%.

~24 hours later, it was -30 basis points lower as the S&P 500 and technology stocks sold off.

Today, yields are back on the rise as equity markets recover.

The ONLY thing that has materially pushed yields lower over the last 2 months has been a downturn in stocks.

Will the Trump Administration soon be forced to pick between the equity and bond market?

item.title: @wallstengine: Tesla just showed its new Roadster prototype driving upside down, flipping in midair and jumping ov...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Tesla just showed its new Roadster prototype driving upside down, flipping in midair and jumping over a lineup of vehicles.
- production targeted for 2028 - 0–60 mph in under 1 second in Tesla’s demonstration - SpaceX-developed cold-gas thrusters for acceleration and flight - A suction system that holds the car against the ramp, even upside down - A claimed top speed of more than 230 mph
The thrusters use compressed air stored in high-pressure tanks that the car can recharge itself.
Tesla lists three versions: Performance, Thrust and the invitation-only, single-seat Rocket with a full flight system.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented export surge across Asia: South Korea’s exports jumpe...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented export surge across Asia:
South Korea’s exports jumped +83.5% YoY in September, the largest annual increase on record and the strongest increase among the major Asian economies.
Furthermore, Singapore’s exports soared +46.2% YoY in August, while Malaysia and Taiwan recorded gains of +45.5% and +41.0% over the same period, respectively.
This was followed by Vietnam’s exports rising +39.1% YoY in September, while China’s exports increased +25.0% YoY in August.
Japan recorded the smallest gains, but its exports still advanced +19.3% YoY in August.
The surge was driven by strong AI-related demand, particularly for semiconductors, electronics, computers, and other technology products.
South Korea’s semiconductor shipments alone jumped +263% YoY in September.
AI demand is fueling a historic surge in Asian exports.
item.content:encoded:
The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented export surge across Asia:

South Korea’s exports jumped +83.5% YoY in September, the largest annual increase on record and the strongest increase among the major Asian economies.

Furthermore, Singapore’s exports soared +46.2% YoY in August, while Malaysia and Taiwan recorded gains of +45.5% and +41.0% over the same period, respectively.

This was followed by Vietnam’s exports rising +39.1% YoY in September, while China’s exports increased +25.0% YoY in August.

Japan recorded the smallest gains, but its exports still advanced +19.3% YoY in August.

The surge was driven by strong AI-related demand, particularly for semiconductors, electronics, computers, and other technology products.

South Korea’s semiconductor shipments alone jumped +263% YoY in September.

AI demand is fueling a historic surge in Asian exports.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Institutional investors are doubling down on tech stocks: 37% of global fund managers are now overw...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Institutional investors are doubling down on tech stocks:
37% of global fund managers are now overweight technology stocks, up from 30% in September, and the highest reading since August 2020, according to a BofA survey of 161 participants overseeing $453 billion in assets.
Technology also has the largest overweight positioning of all sectors.
Pharmaceuticals and Industrials follow, with 23% and 22% overweight, respectively.
On the other hand, 34% of institutional investors are underweight Consumer Discretionary, the sector's most bearish positioning since the 2008 Financial Crisis.
Consumer Staples has the 2nd-most bearish positioning, with 32% of managers underweight.
Institutional investors are doubling down on tech and turning against consumer stocks.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The number of active home sellers in the US rose +1.2% MoM in September, or +17,276, to 1...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The number of active home sellers in the US rose +1.2% MoM in September, or +17,276, to 1,510,784, the highest since March 2020.
At the same time, the number of active homebuyers fell -2.4%, or -23,161, to 928,892, the lowest on record.
This lifts the gap between active sellers and homebuyers to a record 581,892.
As a result, there were +62.6% more home sellers than buyers last month, the largest difference on record.
This percentage has more than doubled since November 2024.
By comparison, the 2021 low was -35.7%, when buyers outnumbered sellers by 633,854.
Hundreds of thousands of homebuyers have been priced-out.

Say you’re using Claude Code or Codex. You connect the vault, set a spending limit, block sites you don’t want it using, and decide which purchases need your approval.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Most people notice a breakdown after the damage is done. A Bullish Formation is a sequence. Higher...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Most people notice a breakdown after the damage is done.
A Bullish Formation is a sequence. Higher Highs and Higher Lows. Every pullback stops above the last one because buyers are stepping in earlier each time.
A Bearish Formation is the mirror. Lower Highs and Lower Lows. Sellers stop waiting for better prices.
The shift between them breaks in the same order every time.
1) Higher Highs stop. That's the setup, not the signal. 2) A Lower High prints. Reduce size. 3) TRADE support gives way. Minimum size. 4) A Lower Low confirms it. By then you should already be out.
The first Lower High is the only clue that arrives BEFORE the price damage.
Go deeper on reading price at https://app.hedgeye.com/education

item.description:
ERP AI is introducing Proto, an AI agent that helps teams build custom business apps from a prompt and then get work done across them.
Teams can create tools for CRM, invoice tracking and inventory, while Proto works across apps and files to update records, generate reports and run workflows.
The goal is to bring software creation and day-to-day tasks into one place, reducing the manual work of moving information between separate tools.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Yesterday, the Nasdaq 100, $NDX, the Semiconductor Index, solana:5XqMbyZbtse5UQUzgrYMpeWLWLR6BWFqUm...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Yesterday, the Nasdaq 100, $NDX, the Semiconductor Index, solana:5XqMbyZbtse5UQUzgrYMpeWLWLR6BWFqUm5H3VAWpump, and the S&P 500 Software Index all fell at least -2.0%, marking just the second trading day in 2026 that all three indexes recorded declines of this magnitude.
This follows 4, 5, and 14 such days in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.
By comparison, there were 34 such trading sessions during the 2022 bear market, 48 in 2000 following the Dot-Com Bubble burst, and 37 in 2008 during the Financial Crisis.
Meanwhile, the Semiconductor Index is now experiencing its 4th correction over the last 135 calendar days, its highest number of corrections within any 135-day period since 2002.
US tech stocks are seeing extreme volatility.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Inflation is RED hot in the US. For anyone not keeping track, US CPI inflation is now nearly double...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Inflation is RED hot in the US.
For anyone not keeping track, US CPI inflation is now nearly double the Fed's 2% target and US PPI Inflation is more than triple that target.
PPI inflation was expected to fall in August, but instead it surged to 6.3%, its second highest level in 4 years.
And, month-over-month Headline PPI inflation surged +1.3%, more than doubling the +0.6% expected and the second largest jump since March 2021.
Meanwhile, month-over-month Core PPI inflation came in +133% above expectations.
The prices Americans are seeing now will look cheap in 12 to 24 months.
All you can do is own assets.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Trading volume in the S&P 500 ETF, $SPY, fell to just 22.6 million shares on Friday, the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Trading volume in the S&P 500 ETF, $SPY, fell to just 22.6 million shares on Friday, the lowest for a full trading day since November 25th, 2005.
Excluding sessions around market holidays, Friday's volume was the lowest since October 11th, 2004.
By comparison, volume fell below 20 million shares on December 24th, 2019, but that was during a half-day trading session.
On Monday, trading volume fell to just ~18 million shares, the lowest non-holiday reading since 2003.
As a result, the 5-day average of $SPY trading activity declined below 30 million shares, its lowest on record.
Meanwhile, the three previous low-volume periods in December 2024, February 2025, and August 2026 were each followed by an S&P 500 pullback.
Markets are in consolidation mode.

While CPI inflation up to 3.7%, inflation is much higher in many crucial categories:
1. Fuel Oil Inflation: +74.2% 2. Gasoline Inflation: +34.2% 3. Airline Fares Inflation: +22.4% 4. Car Repair Inflation: +5.8% 5. Hospital Services Inflation: +5.6% 6. Utility Gas Inflation: +5.0% 7. Electricity Inflation: +4.4% 8. Fruits and Vegetables Inflation: +3.7%
This marks the 67th-straight month with US CPI inflation above the Fed's 2% target.
After 5+ years of persistent inflation, the top 1% of US households are now worth ~14 TIMES the bottom 50%.
Affordability is still getting worse.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Tech stocks are driving the majority of the market's gains this year:
The Information Technology sector is up +36.8% year-to-date, making it the 2nd-best-performing sector in the S&P 500.
It has contributed +10.5 percentage points to the index's +14% gain, the largest contribution of any sector.
Meanwhile, Energy has delivered the strongest return, up +53.3%, but contributed just +1.0 percentage point to the index's gain.
This is followed by Materials, Healthcare, Consumer Staples, and Industrials, which are up +11.0%, +11.0%, +10.5%, and +9.6%, respectively.
Together, these 4 sectors have contributed just +3.0 percentage points to the S&P 500's gain.
Tech is carrying the entire market.

Even amid the rapid scale of AI, open-source models cost far less per token, the basic unit of AI computing.
For example, Anthropic’s Fable 5 model was more than 50 times more expensive per token than DeepSeek’s V4 Pro.
Other open-source models from Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and Nvidia are also competing at a fraction of the cost of leading proprietary models.
As cheaper alternatives improve, proprietary AI companies will face increasing pressure to lower prices.
This could potentially squeeze profit margins all as CapEx is surging.
Keep watching open-source AI.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It's official. US CPI inflation has now been above the Fed's 2% target for 67 consecutive months. T...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It's official.
US CPI inflation has now been above the Fed's 2% target for 67 consecutive months.
The last time inflation was below 2% in the US was in January 2021, amid a global economic lockdown.
Over this period, the value of the US Dollar has declined by -22.5%.
In other words, it now costs $129 to purchase the same goods and services that cost $100 in 2021.
Compounding inflation has become the new norm in the US.
Asset owners are the only winners.

item.title: @wallstengine: $ASML SAYS CHIPMAKERS ARE ALREADY LOOKING TO PLACE EQUIPMENT ORDERS FOR 2029 AND EVEN 2030 CEO Chri...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$ASML SAYS CHIPMAKERS ARE ALREADY LOOKING TO PLACE EQUIPMENT ORDERS FOR 2029 AND EVEN 2030
CEO Christophe Fouquet says “customers are asking us every single day to get more tools,” as AI-related investments drive stronger demand for advanced semiconductor equipment.
The company also outlined major milestones for its next-generation High-NA EUV technology, which Fouquet says is finally approaching high-volume manufacturing after more than a decade of development.
Samsung plans to begin using High-NA EUV in mass production in 2028, followed by TSMC around 2030. Intel is already increasing the number of layers processed and wafer output using the technology.
Separately, ASML plans to introduce its NXE:3800F EUV system in 2027, increasing throughput from 230 to 260 wafers per hour, with a greater impact on customer manufacturing capacity expected from 2028 onward.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Absolutely incredible. Just 10 stocks have driven 70% of the S&P 500’s gain since March 30th. These...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Absolutely incredible.
Just 10 stocks have driven 70% of the S&P 500’s gain since March 30th.
These stocks have added +16 percentage points to the index’s +23% gain over this period.
Nvidia, $NVDA, has contributed the most, accounting for 13% of the S&P 500's gain, or +3 percentage points.
This is followed by Micron, $MU, Apple, $AAPL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, each accounting for 9% of the S&P 500’s advance, adding +2 percentage points.
Return contributions of AMD, $AMD, and Alphabet, $GOOGL, have been 8% and 7%, respectively.
Meanwhile, the remaining 490 stocks have accounted for just 30% of the S&P 500's gain since March 30th, adding +7 percentage points.
Diversification is dead.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The global debt crisis is set to get even worse: The US fiscal deficit is projected to widen to -6....
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The global debt crisis is set to get even worse:
The US fiscal deficit is projected to widen to -6.1% of GDP in 2027, its largest since 2012, excluding the pandemic years of 2020 and 2021.
This will be the biggest deficit as a % of GDP among the 5 major developed economies, including the UK, Germany, France, and Japan.
Furthermore, Germany's deficit is expected to widen from -2.7% of GDP in 2025 to -4.1% in 2027, its largest since 2010, excluding the 2020 pandemic.
Japan's fiscal deficit is estimated to more than triple, from -0.7% to -2.5% of GDP, its largest since 2022.
The UK is the only economy expected to improve its fiscal position, with its deficit narrowing from -4.3% in 2025, to -3.1% of GDP next year, while France's budget gap is projected to widen to -5.2%.
Deficit spending is only accelerating.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US consumer stocks are struggling: The Equal-Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF, $RSPD, is down -8.0...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US consumer stocks are struggling:
The Equal-Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF, $RSPD, is down -8.0% so far in 2026, to near its lowest level since June 2025.
At the same time, the S&P 500 is up +13.9%, and is just 0.3% below its all-time high.
This leaves a massive 22-percentage-point gap in year-to-date performance.
Consumer discretionary stocks are under pressure amid weakening demand, particularly for purchases such as autos, furniture, and home-improvement goods.
At the same time, rising oil prices, elevated inflation, and rising borrowing costs are squeezing household budgets..
As a result, earnings in the Consumer Discretionary and Consumer Staples sectors are expected to decline for the first time since the end of 2024.
Is the consumer running out of money?

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US ETF industry is rapidly expanding:
In total, nearly 1,100 ETFs have launched so far in 2026, up +43% year-over-year.
Leveraged ETFs as a % of total ETFs launched so far in 2026 is up to a record 31.2%.
This percentage has more than quadrupled over the last 3 years.
Furthermore, 48 thematic ETFs were launched in Q3 and 46 in Q2, more than double the previous quarterly record set in Q4 2025.
Thematic ETFs provide investors with targeted exposure to specific trends, industries, technologies, or investment themes such as AI, rather than broad-market indexes.
The ETF market is becoming more specialized and leveraged.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: 14.5% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in September, the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: 14.5% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in September, the highest rate for any September on record.
The only higher readings occurred during the pandemic shock in March and April 2020.
By comparison, between 2017 and 2019, this metric never exceeded 12.0%.
Jacksonville posted the highest cancellation rate last month, at 19.9%, followed by Tampa at 18.8%, Las Vegas at 18.6%, and San Antonio at 18.5%.
In September, home sellers outnumbered buyers by ~63%, the widest gap on record.
US homebuyers are canceling deals at a historic pace.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Shocking stat of the day: The combined wealth of the world’s tech billionaires surged +$845 billion...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Shocking stat of the day:
The combined wealth of the world’s tech billionaires surged +$845 billion in the first 9 months of 2026, the largest increase for this period of the year on record.
This brings the group's combined wealth to a record $4.6 trillion, accounting for 36% of the total wealth tracked by the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.
This is despite tech billionaires representing only ~20% of all members in the index.
For perspective, billionaires outside the technology sector lost a combined -$62 billion over the same period.
Fortunes in the consumer sector fell by -$279 billion, while those in communications declined by -$92 billion.
Americans accounted for 94% of the Bloomberg Billionaires Index's total net wealth gains in the first 9 months of 2026.
As a result, all 10 of the world's richest people have been American since September 10th, the first such occurrence since data began in 2012.
The AI boom is generating unprecedented wealth at the top.

This brings the group's combined wealth to a record $4.6 trillion, accounting for 36% of the total wealth tracked by the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

This is despite tech billionaires representing only ~20% of all members in the index.

For perspective, billionaires outside the technology sector lost a combined -$62 billion over the same period.

Fortunes in the consumer sector fell by -$279 billion, while those in communications declined by -$92 billion.

Americans accounted for 94% of the Bloomberg Billionaires Index's total net wealth gains in the first 9 months of 2026.

As a result, all 10 of the world's richest people have been American since September 10th, the first such occurrence since data began in 2012.

The AI boom is generating unprecedented wealth at the top.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investor demand for trading outside of regular market hours is skyrocketing. In fact, the majority...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investor demand for trading outside of regular market hours is skyrocketing.
In fact, the majority of trading volume in tokenized equities is now occurring OUTSIDE of regular market hours.
BNB Chain has become the first blockchain with over 70% of its tokenized equity trading volume occurring outside of regular market hours.
On Solana, 63% of tokenized equity trading volume is now occurring outside of regular market hours.
Amid this trend, Jupiter, the largest trading platform on Solana, reported +50% month-over-month growth in tokenized asset trading volumes.
As a result, the total circulating supply of tokenized equities has surged to a record $3.3 billion.
Markets are officially becoming 24/7.

item.title: @wallstengine: ScaleDown has launched three specialized AI models for the routine work inside AI agents: classifyi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ScaleDown has launched three specialized AI models for the routine work inside AI agents:
classifying information, extracting data and summarizing documents.
Pricing is $0.05 per million input tokens, with free output.
The goal is to let developers handle these repeatable steps with models built for the job, instead of sending every task to a general-purpose LLM.
1) Classify categorizes inputs, such as support tickets, and returns labels with calibrated probabilities and reasons.
2) Extract pulls information, such as invoice fields, into structured JSON with confidence scores and source citations.
3) Summarize condenses text, images and PDFs into fewer than 1,000 tokens.
The company says the models support a 1 million-token context window for text and images. They are available on platforms including OpenRouter, Vercel and LiteLLM. https://x.com/neal_k_patel/status/2109978626124898587/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global money market funds attracted +$166.4 billion in inflows in the week ending October...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global money market funds attracted +$166.4 billion in inflows in the week ending October 7th, their largest weekly inflow since April 2020.
US money market funds alone posted +$72.3 billion in inflows, lifting their total assets to a record $8.0 trillion.
Since 2023, US money market fund assets have risen +$3.0 trillion.
Meanwhile, global bond funds attracted +$33.8 billion in the week ending October 7th.
Treasury funds accounted for +$16.2 billion, their 15th consecutive weekly inflow and the biggest weekly intake since April 2025.
Investors are piling into risk-free investments as rates surge.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: We are witnessing a historic shift. The annual spread between the S&P 500's earnings yield and the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
We are witnessing a historic shift.
The annual spread between the S&P 500's earnings yield and the 10Y Note yield is down to -1.5 percentage points, its lowest since 2009.
Since 2022, this yield difference has fallen -440 basis points, its largest 5-year decline since the 1970s.
As a result, the S&P 500's equity risk premium is on track to post its 3rd consecutive negative annual reading, the longest streak since 2002.
This suggests that, on a yield basis, theoretically less risky 10Y Treasuries are now more attractive than the S&P 500.
In other words, investors are receiving a higher yield from Treasuries than from the S&P 500, despite the additional risk of owning stocks.
Historically, a negative equity risk premium has been associated with strong risk appetite and stretched equity valuations.
We expect an eventful Q4 ahead.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US bull market is entering its 5th year. Since the October 2022 low, the S&P 500 has rallied +1...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US bull market is entering its 5th year.
Since the October 2022 low, the S&P 500 has rallied +118%, outpacing the average bull market since WWII.
This is also the 3rd-largest gain among bull markets at their 4th anniversary.
Over this period, the index has returned +21.6% in Year 1, +33.7% in Year 2, +12.7% in Year 3, and +19.4% in Year 4.
The average S&P 500 bull market's return since WWII has been +20.8% in Year 5, the 2nd-strongest 12-month performance after +39.1% in Year 1.
Of the 13 previous bull markets, only 6 lasted long enough to reach this stage.
If history is any guide, the market is heading for another year of strong gains.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US stock market has never been this fragmented: The 52-week correlation between the equal-weigh...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US stock market has never been this fragmented:
The 52-week correlation between the equal-weighted S&P 500 and the S&P 500 index is down to 0.67, its lowest level on record.
This measures how closely the performance of the equal-weighted S&P 500 tracks the cap-weighted index, with a lower reading indicating a growing gap between the broader market and mega-cap stocks.
The correlation has declined -0.25 points since August 2025.
By comparison, before the 2020 pandemic, this figure remained between 0.95 and 0.99 for nearly 15 years.
To put this into perspective, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, this metric never declined below 0.85.
The S&P 500 is more concentrated than ever.

item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Flying the coop is getting harder:
49% of adults under 30 live with a parent, up from 37% in 2019.
1 in 4 can’t find work, or can’t find enough of it.
41.5% of recent college graduates work jobs that don’t require their degree.
The median home costs nearly 5x the median household income, compared with 3.2x in the 1990s.
The income needed to buy one rose from $79,600 in 2021 to $126,700 in 2024.
Only 24% of adults under 30 own a home. First-time buyers made up 21% of purchases in NAR’s latest survey, a record low.
Many still lean on family.
59% of parents with kids 18 to 34 gave them money last year.
Among Gen Z and millennial homebuyers, 21% used a cash gift from family for the down payment, and 18% lived with family to save for it.
Moving out now takes a job, and often a parent's wallet.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META LAUNCHES MUSE WONDER FOR PERSONAL AI AGENTS AND CODING
Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, calling them its most capable models yet. Both were trained at its gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center.
The series combines Active Memory, which carries relevant context across conversations, with Active Focus, designed to keep agents working through complex tasks, trying alternative approaches and checking with users before important actions.
The models target personal assistance and professional workflows, including software development and tasks involving legal, financial and health information. Meta reports state-of-the-art results across benchmarks for agents, memory and coding.
For developers, the coding capabilities focus on sustained work across projects: tracking requirements, changing multiple parts of a codebase, testing results and making revisions.
Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code. Muse Wonder Full is available to Muse Code subscribers.
Muse Wonder will also roll out to the Muse app, starting with subscribers, and power artifact generation and other tasks requiring more advanced capabilities.
Meta says the models include stronger safeguards for private information, malicious instructions and misuse. A fuller safety report is expected later. https://x.com/finkd/status/2109689307288240154/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The global rate hike cycle is here. 15 of the 33 major central banks, or 45%, have raised interest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The global rate hike cycle is here.
15 of the 33 major central banks, or 45%, have raised interest rates over the last 6 months, the largest proportion since 2023.
This figure is now approaching the ~55%, recorded in 2018 and 2011.
By comparison, the proportion peaked at ~95% in 2022, following post-pandemic stimulus and the resulting surge in global inflation.
In total, 54 central banks have hiked rates so far in 2026.
This also marks the first time since September 2023 that more central banks have hiked than cut rates over a rolling 3-month period.
"Higher for longer" is back.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA OPENS VERA RUBIN RACK DESIGNS, EXPANDS AI NETWORKING WITH META, GOOGLE AND CISCO NVIDIA annou...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA OPENS VERA RUBIN RACK DESIGNS, EXPANDS AI NETWORKING WITH META, GOOGLE AND CISCO
NVIDIA announced new partnerships and open infrastructure contributions at the OCP Global Summit, covering rack designs, networking, software and power systems for next-generation AI data centers.
The company contributed key Vera Rubin rack and compute tray designs through its MGX architecture. The updated MGX 1.2 specification supports racks up to 250kW, with standardized power connections, liquid cooling and fanless compute trays.
$META is adopting NVIDIA’s Spectrum-6 Ethernet switches, which deliver 102.4Tb/s of switching capacity. Combined with Spectrum-X Multiplane technology, the architecture is designed to connect more than 100,000 GPUs with fewer switch layers. Traffic is distributed across up to eight independent network paths, allowing workloads to keep running if a component fails.
Cisco $CSCO and NVIDIA announced plans for USFP, a new pluggable optical module designed for 400Gb/s-per-lane networking. The companies say it will deliver 4x the bandwidth density and approximately 1.3x the power efficiency of 200Gb/s-per-lane modules, with up to 12.8Tb/s of overall capacity in roughly the same physical footprint.
TE Connectivity and Amphenol are helping develop USFP connectors, cages and modules. The companies plan to establish an open industry specification, giving multiple suppliers a common design to build around.
Google’s Falcon Transport will be supported on future NVIDIA ConnectX-10 SuperNICs and BlueField DPUs. The collaboration enables NVIDIA and Google networking hardware to communicate over a common transport, with features for managing congestion, recovering dropped packets and protecting connections.
NVIDIA also released new open-source DSX software components for configuring networks, stress-testing GPU clusters, managing racks and preparing hardware for deployment. Its Vera CPU rack design specifically targets AI agent workloads, including tool calling, orchestration and sandboxed execution.
On power infrastructure, NVIDIA joined AMD, Google and Meta on an open data-center design specification, and Google, Meta and Microsoft on grid-resilience standards.
Separately, Visionbay introduced plans for K-1, an 800V DC AI factory platform combining NVIDIA’s reference architecture with Vertiv’s power and cooling technologies for future Vera Rubin deployments.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted +$30.7 billion in inflows in Q3 2026, their la...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted +$30.7 billion in inflows in Q3 2026, their largest quarterly intake on record.
In September, inflows totaled +$10 billion, the 3rd-largest monthly inflow of 2026, following +$17.9 billion in August, the 2nd-largest monthly intake on record.
As a result, global gold ETF holdings rose +67 tonnes last month to a record 4,256 tonnes.
This surpasses the previous record of 4,176 tonnes set in February.
Year-to-date, global gold ETFs have seen +$38.5 billion in inflows, equivalent to an increase of +226 tonnes in gold holdings, with all regions recording positive demand.
UK-listed funds have attracted +$9.5 billion in inflows over the same period, overtaking China to become the largest source of country-level demand so far in 2026.
Demand for gold is extremely strong.

Initially wholly owned by Ondas, Regna will use Palantir’s AI platform and model-training infrastructure. Ondas will also be its first customer.

Signals and fractals are the foundation of @hedgeye - and the principal reason why Hedgeye is our only outside resource. (If you cherish your hard earned capital I suggest you too should consider subscribing).
But sometimes forgotten is the strength of Hedgeye's research team of 40 analysts.
Case in point: in late 2022, Hedgeye's team (led by Rob Simone) wrote a negative research report on Medical Properties Trust ($MPT) which was trading at about $15/share at the time. I had never heard of the REIT.
Prompted by Rob's comprehensive analysis we @seabreezelop followed up with our own research and shorted the stock back then (at about $15.40).
We remain short and the shares are trading at about $3.
Kudos.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US seasonal hiring is off to a weak start: US-based employers announced plans to hire 90,787 worker...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US seasonal hiring is off to a weak start:
US-based employers announced plans to hire 90,787 workers in September, the weakest September total since 2011.
This marks a -23% decline from the 117,313 recorded in September 2025.
Retail led all industries last month, with 65,150 announced hires, followed by Aerospace and Defense at 5,300.
However, announced seasonal hiring is muted so far this year, with a combined 62,000 seasonal hires, compared with 100,800 announced by seasonal employers last September.
Year-to-date, US hiring plans have totaled 210,612 workers, the 2nd-lowest total for the first 9 months of the year in at least 10 years.
Retail leads all sectors with 66,557 announcements so far in 2026, followed by Technology, at 22,361, and Aerospace and Defense, at 21,841.
Hiring demand remains muted.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The gap between AI names and the rest of the market is historic: Since the start of 2024, a basket...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The gap between AI names and the rest of the market is historic:
Since the start of 2024, a basket of 42 AI stocks has generated 67% of the S&P 500's price return.
In other words, those names have contributed +22 percentage points to the index’s +33% gain over this period.
By comparison, the remaining 458 stocks have added +11 percentage points.
Additionally, those 42 AI stocks have accounted for 58% of the S&P 500's earnings growth and 81% of CapEx and R&D growth since the start of 2024.
The rest of the index has therefore contributed just 20% of total CapEx and R&D growth over the same period.
Meanwhile, just 29% of stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 over the last 3 years, close to the ~25% low recorded during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.
AI is all that matters.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US families are falling behind on debt payments. The percentage of families reporting overdue loan...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US families are falling behind on debt payments.
The percentage of families reporting overdue loan payments surged to 19.6% in 2025, the highest since 2010, according to the Fed data.
This marks a sharp increase from 12.2% recorded in 2022.
This also reverses the gradual improvement between 2013 and 2019, when the percentage declined by -2.6 points.
Furthermore, more than 8.0% of families reported they were at least 2 months behind on payments, up from 5.0% in 2022.
This comes despite the typical family debt load remaining unchanged since 2022, suggesting that more households are struggling to keep up with existing financial obligations.
Americans are falling behind on loan payments at a concerning pace.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The Bank of Japan's total assets declined -$98 billion in Q3 2026, to $3.95 trillion, the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Bank of Japan's total assets declined -$98 billion in Q3 2026, to $3.95 trillion, the lowest since Q1 2020.
Since the Q1 2024 peak, the BoJ has reduced its balance sheet by -$828 billion, or -17.4%.
As a result, the BoJ's Asset-to-GDP ratio has fallen -28 percentage points over this period, to 94%, the lowest since 2018.
Furthermore, Japanese government bond holdings fell -$90 billion in Q3, to $3.19 trillion, the lowest since Q1 2020.
Since the 2023 peak, JGB holdings have dropped -$556 billion, or -14.9%.
The BoJ also sold -$568 million in equity ETFs and J-REITs last quarter, bringing its holdings down to $233 billion, the lowest since Q3 2021.
The Bank of Japan continues to unwind its balance sheet.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: China’s industrial profit growth is losing momentum: China’s industrial profits rose +4.2% YoY in A...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China’s industrial profit growth is losing momentum:
China’s industrial profits rose +4.2% YoY in August, the weakest YoY growth since November 2025.
This also marks the 4th consecutive monthly slowdown in growth.
Pressure is particularly visible in consumer-facing industries, where profits are falling in autos, clothing, and furniture.
Domestic demand continues to weaken, with consumption growth slowing to near zero while manufacturers, property developers, and infrastructure builders are cutting spending.
For the first 8 months of 2026, industrial profits were still up +15.7% YoY, but the gains are becoming increasingly concentrated, with the electronics industry contributing ~66% of total growth.
At the same time, raw-material industries contributed +6.2 percentage points to the overall increase, supported by higher commodity prices.
Weak domestic demand is weighing on China’s economy.

China’s industrial profits rose +4.2% YoY in August, the weakest YoY growth since November 2025.

This also marks the 4th consecutive monthly slowdown in growth.

Pressure is particularly visible in consumer-facing industries, where profits are falling in autos, clothing, and furniture.

Domestic demand continues to weaken, with consumption growth slowing to near zero while manufacturers, property developers, and infrastructure builders are cutting spending.

For the first 8 months of 2026, industrial profits were still up +15.7% YoY, but the gains are becoming increasingly concentrated, with the electronics industry contributing ~66% of total growth.

At the same time, raw-material industries contributed +6.2 percentage points to the overall increase, supported by higher commodity prices.

Weak domestic demand is weighing on China’s economy.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US deficit is surging despite low unemployment. The cumulative US fiscal deficit since 2020 has...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US deficit is surging despite low unemployment.
The cumulative US fiscal deficit since 2020 has surged to a massive $14.18 trillion.
Meanwhile, the 7-year average unemployment rate has fallen -0.4 percentage points, to 4.7% over the same period.
In the first 11 months of FY2026 alone, the US deficit totaled $1.97 trillion, the 3rd-largest for this period of the year in history.
When the economy is strong and unemployment is low, the government would typically keep fiscal deficits lower, reserving large-scale fiscal support for periods of economic weakness.
This time, however, the deficit is running at historically high levels despite stable unemployment.
This comes as elevated government spending and rising interest costs are keeping the deficit exceptionally large even without a recession.
Massive deficits have become a permanent feature of the US economy.
